hints.title: Directed Cycle and Two-Parent Conflict Obstacle
hints.text: Adding one directed edge to a rooted tree can cause a node to have two incoming edges, introduce a directed cycle, or both. How can dissecting whether two parent edges exist pinpoint which edge breaks tree structure?

hints.title: Dual Edge Candidate Classification Invariant
hints.text: If any node receives two incoming edges, one of those two candidate edges must be removed. Otherwise, the redundant edge is simply the edge that introduces a directed cycle.

hints.title: Candidate Pruning and Disjoint Set Verification Procedure
hints.text: First inspect edges to see if any node has two incoming edges; if so, record cand1 and cand2. Next, process edges using a disjoint set data structure while skipping cand2. If a cycle forms during union operations, return cand1 if two incoming edges existed, otherwise return the cycle-causing edge. If no cycle forms after skipping cand2, then cand2 is the redundant edge.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of vertices/edges in the directed graph
complexity.notes: Scans edges to identify two-parent candidates then performs at most N DSU union operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every edge removal with full tree DFS takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Parent mapping and DSU array consume O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Carefully distinguishing between two-parent nodes, simple cycles, and cycles containing two-parent nodes.
